invariants: Exactly one Local Administrator authentication identity exists per installation; Contacts never authenticate.
Authentication credentials, live-data encryption keys, portable-backup recovery material and run-auth identities are cryptographically and lifecycle-distinct authorities.
Changing the administrator password does not redefine operational identity or require treating that password as the live-data key.
Portable restore performs complete verification before modifying live authoritative data.
Loopback, PID, port or registry presence alone never establishes trusted SOMA instance identity.
Only the process that owns the canonical data instance and passes authenticated run verification may be controlled as the active SOMA host.
Reusable device/authentication secrets never enter ordinary domain, evidence, Notes, workbook, audit payload, diagnostic, console, CI, crash or support-output state.
Beta 1.0 exposes no device credential or SSH control and has no local secret fallback for future external credential-provider failure.
Diagnostic records are non-authoritative and cannot satisfy or replace domain audit/history requirements.
Diagnostic emission failure cannot convert migration, audit, authorization, integrity or domain transaction failure into success.
Sensitive diagnostic data is prevented at the call site and sanitized before queuing; sanitizer failure omits data and never emits raw fallback.
Hashing, encryption, encoding, truncation or partial display does not by itself make sensitive material safe to log.
SOMA performs no automatic support/diagnostic upload in Beta 1.0.
Security-sensitive startup, shutdown and restore decisions use fresh bounded revalidation rather than stale registry/UI state.
acceptance_hooks: wildcard-bind, proxy/redirect, PID/port-reuse and forged-registry rejection scenarios
diagnostic secret/body canary scenarios including nested/encoded/truncated forms
diagnostic-writer failure leaves authoritative outcome unchanged scenario
